national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said that India’s economic strength and resilience have been built over the past decade through a combination of fiscal prudence, infrastructure investment, banking reforms, improved delivery mechanisms and consistent reforms. Addressing the 5th Kautilya economic conclave in New Delhi, the Finance Minister said that the government has advanced the national frameworks through GST, insolvency and bankruptcy code and the four labour codes. She said that India had navigated the shocks of the past four years with its fundamentals intact, citing 7.8 percent real GDP growth in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27. The Finance Minister said that the IMF projects India’s general government debt to decline from 83.4 percent of GDP in 2026 to 77.7 percent in 2031 against a rising global trend. On infrastructure development, Ms Sitharaman said, capital expenditure for this fiscal had been budgeted at 12.22 lakh crore rupees. She added that the national highway network had expanded by about 61 per cent and the number of operational airports had more than doubled since 2014. She also highlighted that more than 52 crore collateral-free loans have been sanctioned under PM MUDRA Yojana. Highlighting the PM Awas Yojana, PM Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, Ms Sitaharaman said that these initiatives have strengthened citizens’ capacity to participate in growth and build capacities to fight the challenges.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | Sports 28 Asian Games: India wins five gold, two silver, two bronze medals today; Climbs to fourth place in...
national_raw_news.content: India won five gold, two silver and two bronze medals at the Asian Games in Japan today. In Hockey, India thrashed Malaysia 5-1 to defend their men’s gold and the triumph also secured them a direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. For India, captain Harmanpreet Singh netted two goals while Jugraj, Hardik and Shilanand scored one goal each. In Men’s Cricket, India won the gold defeating arch-rivals Pakistan by 19 runs in the T20 final at Nisshin. Wrestler Aman Sehrawat clinched the men’s 57kg gold after edging out North Korea’s world champion Chong Song Han 11-7 in a fierce final. Kumkum Mohod won the individual gold medal in the women’s recurve archery event. In Golf, Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games gold medal in the women’s individual title. India also bagged silver in the team event. Wrestler Antim Panghal sealed a silver medal in the women’s 53 kg category. Deepak Punia won bronze in the men’s 97kg freestyle wrestling event after defeating Mongolia’s Gankhuyag Ganbaatar. Archer Neeraj Chauhan got bronze in the men’s individual recurve event. With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fourth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 85, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals.
